page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent data.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains in the average tier, though the PassMark memory score is weak. Text processing performance is poor, placing in the bottom 10%, while database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations achieve average throughput.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as a compute-oriented option. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power, but the lack of local storage and weak single-core performance are notable tradeoffs. The instance offers moderate multi-core efficiency for workloads that can parallelize across its 16 vCPUs, though memory-bound tasks may experience bottlenecks due to the lower memory-per-core ratio and weak memory benchmark scores.

The ecs.n1.3xlarge is suitable for multi-threaded applications that do not require high single-core performance or massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, parallel software compilation, basic database operations, and distributed caching systems like Redis.
